prompt: Review the uncommitted change in this repository against `docs/contracts/retry.md`. Return ONLY a JSON array of findings: [{"code": "<concise stable defect code>", "blocking": true|false, "evidence": "<the file and line you read, or the command you ran and what it printed>"}]. Report only what you have evidence for: this diff is two lines, and a review that lists more than it can show is as unusable as one that lists nothing. This is a read-only task: report what you found and change no file in the repository.

source.note: A two-line diff swapping `??` for `||`, so a caller-supplied zero silently becomes the default -- the smallest real defect this project could find that still has a contract to violate. Written for #174: the trivial tier was empty for all eight roles while the profile assigned a model to every one of them. A trivial task answers one question, whether the cheapest model is adequate, so it must still measure restraint: the fixture keeps a tempting non-defect (an optional parameter documented as optional) and the scorer requires exactly one blocking finding, because a reviewer that reports two findings on a two-line diff is unusable however cheap it is. Calibrated before committing and SATURATED: glm-5.3-flash, deepseek-v4.1-flash and minimax-m3 all score 1.00 twice, the cheapest at $0.0007 per run. That is the answer the trivial tier exists to give -- on a review this small the cheapest model on the provider is adequate -- so the task is `smoke` and its score is never quoted as evidence about a model. It also found the defect this corpus keeps producing: five of the six runs before it shipped scored exactly 0.57, and the artifact showed a model that had identified the defect, cited the contract and PROVEN it by evaluating the changed expression, coded `zero-retry-count-broken-by-falsy-fallback` -- while the check's word list lacked 'falsy fallback'.
